paragraphs.text: translated by
1. WHEN, Vasu, wilt thou love the laud? Now let the channel bring the stream.
paragraphs.original: कदा वसो स्तोत्रं हर्यत आव श्मशा रुधद्वाः ।
paragraphs.translit: kadā vaso stotraṃ haryata āva śmaśā rudhadvāḥ |

paragraphs.text: The juice is ready to ferment.
2. He whose two Bay Steeds harnessed well, swerving, pursue the Bird's tail-plumes,
paragraphs.original: हरी यस्य सुयुजा विव्रता वेरर्वन्तानु शेपा ।
paragraphs.translit: harī yasya suyujā vivratā verarvantānu śepā |

paragraphs.text: With Rowing manes, like heaven and earth, he is the Lord with power to give.
3. Bereft of skill is Indra, if, like some outwearied man he fears
paragraphs.original: अप योरिन्द्रः पापज आ मर्तो न शश्रमाणो बिभीवान् ।
paragraphs.translit: apa yorindraḥ pāpaja ā marto na śaśramāṇo bibhīvān |

paragraphs.text: The sinner, when the Mighty hath prepared himself for victory.
4. Indra with these drives round, until he meets with one to worship him:
Indra is Master of the pair who snort and swerve upon their way.
5. Borne onward by the long-maned Steeds who stretch themselves as 'twere for food,
paragraphs.original: अधि यस्तस्थौ केशवन्ता व्यचस्वन्ता न पुष्ट्यै ।
paragraphs.translit: adhi yastasthau keśavantā vyacasvantā na puṣṭyai |

paragraphs.text: The God who wears the helm defends them with his jaws.
6. The Mighty sang with Lofty Ones: the Hero fashioned with his strength,
Like skillful Matarisvan with his power and might,
7. The bolt, which pierced at once the vitals of the Dasyu easy to be slain,
paragraphs.original: वज्रं यश्चक्रे सुहनाय दस्यवे हिरीमशो हिरीमान् ।
paragraphs.translit: vajraṃ yaścakre suhanāya dasyave hirīmaśo hirīmān |

paragraphs.text: With jaw uninjured like the wondrous firmament.
8. Grind off our sins: with song will we conquer the men who sing no hymns:
Not easily art thou pleased with prayerless sacrifice.
9. When threefold flame burns high for thee, to rest on poles of sacrifice,
paragraphs.original: ऊर्ध्वा यत्ते त्रेतिनी भूद्यज्ञस्य धूर्षु सद्मन् ।
paragraphs.translit: ūrdhvā yatte tretinī bhūdyajñasya dhūrṣu sadman |

paragraphs.text: Thou with the living joyest in the self-bright Ship.
10. Thy glory was the speckled cup, thy glory was the flawless scoop.
Wherewith thou pourest into thy receptacle.
11. As hundreds, O Immortal God, have sung to thee, so hath Sumitra, yea, Durmitra praised thee here,
paragraphs.original: शतं वा यदसुर्य प्रति त्वा सुमित्र इत्थास्तौद्दुर्मित्र इत्थास्तौत् ।
paragraphs.translit: śataṃ vā yadasurya prati tvā sumitra itthāstauddurmitra itthāstaut |

paragraphs.text: What time thou holpest Kutsa's son, when Dasyus fell, yea, holpest Kutsa's darling when the Dasyus died.
paragraphs.original: आवो यद्दस्युहत्ये कुत्सपुत्रं प्रावो यद्दस्युहत्ये कुत्सवत्सम्
paragraphs.translit: āvo yaddasyuhatye kutsaputraṃ prāvo yaddasyuhatye kutsavatsam
